lib/segment/src/types.rs lines 3834-3866:

#[derive(
    Debug, Deserialize, Serialize, JsonSchema, Validate, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Default, Hash,
)]
#[serde(deny_unknown_fields, rename_all = "snake_case")]
pub struct Filter {
    /// At least one of those conditions should match
    #[validate(nested)]
    #[serde(
        default,
        with = "MaybeOneOrMany",
        skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none"
    )]
    #[schemars(with = "MaybeOneOrMany<Condition>")]
    pub should: Option<Vec<Condition>>,
    /// At least minimum amount of given conditions should match
    #[validate(nested)]
    #[serde(skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
    pub min_should: Option<MinShould>,
    /// All conditions must match
    #[validate(nested)]
    #[serde(
        default,
        with = "MaybeOneOrMany",
        skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none"
    )]
    #[schemars(with = "MaybeOneOrMany<Condition>")]
    pub must: Option<Vec<Condition>>,
    /// All conditions must NOT match
    #[validate(nested)]
    #[serde(
        default,
        with = "MaybeOneOrMany",
        skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none"
    )]
    #[schemars(with = "MaybeOneOrMany<Condition>")]
    pub must_not: Option<Vec<Condition>>,  // ← MUST be Vec<Condition>, not single Condition
}

source_grounding.note: Root cause: The Filter struct uses `serde(with = "MaybeOneOrMany")` for must_not/must/should fields. This serde wrapper is designed to accept both single items and arrays for convenience, BUT for filter conditions, the API specification requires an array (Vec<Condition>). The MaybeOneOrMany wrapper silently accepts a single Condition object and auto-wraps it into a Vec, bypassing validation that should reject non-array input. This is a true Type1_IllegalSuccess - the API accepts semantically malformed requests (single object instead of array) that violate the explicit type contract Vec<Condition>.
